w: Swamishri inaugurated and performed the murti-pratishtha of the Swaminarayan Mandir, Sankari

To do little and gain more is a gambler's tendency. To do wrong work and gain more money is a gambler's tendency. To labor for less than 8 hours at work or business and desire for more money is a gambler's tendency.
To take more in return for less effort does not please God.

In the evening Kishore Day assembly, the kishores performed an impressive folkdance on the glory of the Swaminarayan Mahamantra and a drama 'Hraday hraday na setu'. In conclusion, Swamishri addressed the kishores emphasizing the need and importance of satsang.

2006.o: Yagna for World Peace, Nagar Yatra
w: The yagna, under the auspices of the pratishtha rituals, had 1501 participants (Yajmans) seated around 187 yagna kunds with 110 Brahmins pundits performing the rituals. There were an additional 11 main yagna kunds on stage with 105 participants. Swamishri performed the panchamrut rituals on Shri Harikrishna Maharaj and thereafter he blessed the assembly, “The yagna has commenced for the murti-pratishtha ceremony. It is also a yagna for world peace. Hindu dharma is very charitable and perseveres for the good of all. It seeks to elevate and bestow moksha to all animals and humans. People may say that there is no peace in India. But to live amidst difficulties is indeed God’s grace and protection. By performing such yagnas we seek to be blessed with God’s grace, happiness and to become brahmarup...” Swamishri then performed the pujan and arti rituals of the murtis to be installed in the shikharbaddh mandir, namely, Akshar Purushottam Maharaj, Ghanshyam Maharaj, Harikrishna Maharaj, Radha Krishna Dev, Ram Panchayatan, Shiv Panchayatan and Guru Parampara. Twenty-one thousand devotees and well-wishers came for darshan of the yagna and partook of the mahaprasad.

At 4.30 pm a grand procession (nagar yatra) of the murtis was carried out on the streets of Bhavnagar. The colourful pageant of devotion and its various attractions attracted the city dwellers, inspiring joy and devotion in their hearts.

Prior to the grand murti-pratishtha ceremony day of BAPS Swaminarayan Mandir, Bhadra, a yagna for World Peace was held from 9.00 a.m. In the evening a colourful procession of the murtis was held in the village. See details in Swaminarayan Bliss, June 2010.
